title: Priority bucket exchange — midweek ops and kernel/kvcache sync
body:
Context and goal:
This note captures midweek standup discussion (Jun 18) focused on the priority-bucket experiment that ties kernel handshake changes to KV-cache shadowing and a cohort-based prioritizer for batching. Goal: reduce p50 and p95 latency regressions during small-tail bursts while keeping GPU utilization efficient and not increasing token cost by more than 3%.

Top-level summary:
- Kernel interface refactor (handshake + queue token): branch kernel-handshake-v2 now implements explicit request metadata (priority_hint, cohort_id) and a non-blocking ack path. Initial integration tests passed in CI (unit + small end-to-end).
- KV-cache shadowing: ran a 6-hour shadow job in us-west with LRUV eviction (LRU + variable TTL per cohort) — hit steady hit-rate +8% for conversational cohorts, slight headroom pressure on large-sequence cohorts.
- Batching/cohort prioritizer: new priority-bucket exchange algorithm that splits incoming queue into (fast-path, steady, background) buckets. Micro-batching reduced p95 for fast-path by ~22% under synthetic 10k rps spike.
- Observed tradeoffs: improved tail latency for small-context requests, cost neutral overall in default workload; background bucket experienced higher completion latency (expected) — we need explicit backfill policies for delayed requests.

Metrics snapshot (baseline vs experiment):
- p50 latency (fast-path): baseline 18ms -> experiment 14ms
- p95 latency (fast-path): baseline 120ms -> experiment 94ms
- overall token cost delta: +0.8% (within target)
- KV hit rate (conv cohorts): baseline 42% -> experiment 50%
- GPU util change: baseline 68% -> experiment 71% (with slightly more short-lived kernels)

Kernel refactor status:
- What changed: handshake now carries priority_hint (0..3), cohort_id string, and optional prefetch_ok flag. The runtime scheduler can accept a non-blocking ack to allow queue shuffling without head-of-line blocking.
- Tests added: unit tests for handshake parsing, fuzz test for malformed metadata, integration smoke for routing into priority buckets.
- Known regressions: when priority_hint is missing, legacy fallback path activates but currently adds ~6ms overhead; capture ticket INF-4339 to remove legacy parsing cost in next patch.
- Next steps: land PR #1287 (review comments addressed) + deploy canary on bowl-03 for 24h, then validate with synthetic spike harness.

KV-cache shadowing and LRUV experiment:
- Rationale: some cohorts (short-turn convs) benefit disproportionately from longer TTLs; a pure LRU was evicting those keys too aggressively during bursts. LRUV = LRU + cohort-weighted TTL.
- Shadow job findings: conv-cohort keys TTL extended from 60s -> 180s gave better reuse. Hit rate +8% but memory pressure rose by ~3% in shadow pool.
- Oddity observed: large-sequence cohorts (batch infer jobs) created fragmented KV entries that inflated bookkeeping cost — adding a soft cap per-cohort reduced fragmentation.
- Action: prototype per-cohort soft-cap and dynamic TTL tuning in kvcache-controller (Rashid/Aisha), target rollout in canary cluster after PR review.

Batching and cohort prioritizer details:
- Priority buckets: fast-path (latency-sensitive small seq), steady (normal requests), background (heavy/low-priority). Buckets are sized by dynamic sampling of incoming seq length + recent completion time distributions.
- Sampling strategy: random 1% sampler that records seq length and completion latencies to update bucket thresholds every minute.
- Micro-batching change: allow fast-path to form batches up to 12 tokens or 8 requests whichever hits first; previously fixed at 6 requests. This avoids head-of-line waits for a single long request.
- Observed behavior: under synthetic spike of short requests, fast-path p95 dropped ~22%; background p95 rose (by design).
- Risk: bursts with mixed long/short sequences still cause some jitter; need smarter requeue for long-tail requests.

Synthetic load test summary (us-west canaries):
- Setup: 10k rps synthetic mix (70% short convs, 20% medium, 10% long seq), run 6 hours across 3 canaries.
- Results: priority-bucket strategy kept service availability >99.98%. Measured end-to-end p50/p95 improvements as above. No OOMs. Slight increase in short-lived kernel churn logged.
- Observability notes: added new tags to tracing (bucket_id, cohort_id, kvcache_hit) to make postmortem easier.

Operational concerns and open questions:
- Backpressure for background bucket: do we accept dropping background requests or always queue and risk latency explosion? Proposal: soft-defer + retry policy with exponential backoff; need SRE opinion.
- Billing attribution: micro-batching changes can alter per-request token attribution in analytics; product asked for a short doc on how to interpret cost signals.
- Long-sequence fragmentation: how to avoid kv indexing blowup from batch inference; tentative soft-cap per cohort seems promising but needs stress tests.

Decisions made this sync:
- Proceed with canary rollout of kernel-handshake-v2 + priority-buckets on bowl-03 and bowl-05 for 24h (Aisha to schedule).
- Enable LRUV shadowing in shadow pool only (do not promote to production yet).
- Add tracing tags in tracer-agent and push a dashboard tile for bucket-level latency.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Aisha: land PR #1287, coordinate canary deploy (ETA: 2029-06-20)
- Benji: implement per-cohort soft-cap prototype for kvcache-controller, push perf numbers (ETA: 2029-06-24)
- Liu Wei: add exponential backoff proposal & SLO impact analysis, sync with SRE (ETA: 2029-06-21)
- Sofia: cost-attribution brief for product analytics (ETA: 2029-06-23)
- Rashid: run extended 24h LRUV shadow with mixed workload and report memory/cost (ETA: 2029-06-25)

Blockers and help needed:
- Infra: need temporary increased shadow kvcache quota on bowl-shdw-1 for extended shadow tests (infra ticket created).
- SRE: input on safe de-prioritization semantics for background bucket (requesting a short review).

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Keep experiment IDs in spans (exp=priority-buckets-v1) for easier filtering.
- Watch for increased kernel churn alerts; add an ephemeral alert to detect >15% increase in short-lived kernel starts over 5min window.

Meeting follow-ups planned:
- Friday retro: share canary results and decide on promoting LRUV to production or iterating TTL heuristics.
- Deep-dive next Tuesday: batching heuristics and queue requeue strategy with SRE present.

End of midweek log.

-- Aisha
